name: Property manager

pf.license.need: Where the state's form says managing rentals for others needs a license (often a real estate broker's license), the business's own license. Each leasing agent's own license or registration, only where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.maintenance staff: No license for the work they're booked for. Work that needs a licensed trade (a gas line, an electrical panel, a roof, structural work) is never booked with them.
pf.license.ask: The business's license number, or its registration where no license is needed. Each leasing agent's number in their invite reply, where the state's form asks for one.
pf.license.who holds it: The business, under its managing broker where the state's form says so; each leasing agent, where the form says so.
pf.license.how it's checked: none: Rosie never looks up, checks or confirms a license, insurance or registration (D96); anything shown is as given by the business, not checked by Rosie
pf.license.blocks going live: Where the state's form says a license is needed and none checks out, the work stays offline in that state. A leasing agent whose license is needed and isn't active is never offered.
pf.license.renewals: Checked on each renewal date from the state's form. A lapse pauses that person's bookings, and Sam is told.
pf.license.insurance: Any insurance or bond the state's form asks for, on file before going live.
pf.license.background check: None through Rosie. Any check the business runs on its own staff is its own.
pf.license.shown to customers: The business's name, and any license number the state's rules say to show, from the state's form. Example numbers use a made-up format, like EX-1042.

pf.services.pattern: Consult: time with a leasing agent, a self-guided tour window, a spot at an open house, or a maintenance visit by the business's own staff. Every service is free to the person booking. Every booking names one property from the business's own list of the properties and units it manages: a tour, an open house spot or a maintenance visit is booked for a listed property only.

pf.services.questions, not a booking: Questions about available homes are answered only from the business's own listing details: the rent as listed, the date it's free, its size, the pet rules, parking, and how to apply the business's own way. Everyone gets the same answer.
pf.services.never booked in Rosie: Rental applications, screening, credit or background checks, leases, rent, deposits, fees, resident notices, move-in or move-out paperwork, and sending outside vendors. The business keeps its own tools for all of that.
pf.services.repairs never booked with staff: Work that needs a licensed trade. Rosie passes it to the office, which arranges it its own way.
pf.services.capacity: One leasing agent per tour, for the person and up to 3 other adults; children who come along are never counted or asked about. One group per self-guided window. Open house spots up to the business's cap. One maintenance tech per visit.
pf.services.travel area: Each booking names one property from the business's own list of properties and units it manages (a tour, an open house spot or a maintenance visit). Only listed homes are booked; the portal holds the list.
pf.services.booking window: Tours up to 30 days ahead, with at least 1 hour's notice. Self-guided tours need 2 hours, for the ID check. Repairs up to 14 days ahead, soonest first. These are the example business's settings.
pf.services.blocked times: Staff calendars. A home that's leased comes off the list at once. A home's self-guided windows close while staff work in it.

before times: A tour: which home? It must be on the business's own list. Rosie never suggests, ranks or rules out homes or areas.
A tour: with a leasing agent, self-guided, by video, or at an open house?
A tour: when would you like to move in? It only narrows homes that are free by then.
A repair: which town? Rosie checks the business manages homes there; the street address and unit go only on the secure page, where the home is checked against the business's list.
A repair: what needs fixing, in your own words? Every answer gets the danger check.
after a time is picked: A tour: anything that helps the tour, like a step-free way in?
An open house: how many in your group? A number only.
A repair: will you be home, or may staff go in while you're out?
A repair: any pets? They must be put away for the visit.
only on the secure page: A photo ID check before a self-guided tour, and before a tour with an agent where the business turns that on. Only the business sees the result.
The one-time door code for a self-guided tour, shown only in the booked window
Permission to enter while nobody is home, signed by a resident on the business's list for that home
Entry details for staff: which key, an alarm code, where a pet is kept
A request for a disability accommodation: a box that goes to a person at the business
Is it safe to text you?
pf.questions.never asked: Race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, family or children, or any other protected trait. Income, credit or rental history: that's the business's own application. Who will live in the home.
pf.questions.who may book: A tour: any adult, the same way for everyone. A repair: a resident on the business's list for that home, or the owner or someone the business names. Permission to enter: only a resident on that list. A teen at home: an adult resident books.

words that stop a booking: 911 now: a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm going off
a lockout with a child or a pet inside (911, then the business's emergency line)
words that stop a booking: the business': water flooding, or coming through a ceiling
pf.safety.crisis words: The 988 line first, for every kind of work.

what Rosie says.gas, fire, smoke or an alarm: Leave the home now and call 911 from outside. Don't use switches or flames. Then call the emergency line.
what Rosie says.flooding or no heat in freezing weather: Call the emergency line now. Nothing is booked by text for this.
what Rosie says.a lockout with a child or pet inside: Call 911 now, then the emergency line.

pf.safety.not danger: One short chirp every minute or so from an alarm is a low battery: a repair visit is booked. An alarm that keeps sounding is danger.
pf.safety.fair housing, on every message: Words that would steer ('safe area', 'good schools', 'families', 'what kind of people live there'): Rosie gives no opinion, points to public sources, and books any home the person names. A question about a protected trait is never answered with an opinion, and never changes what anyone is offered.
pf.safety.staff safety: The check-in code proves who came. After a tour, DONE closes it; with no DONE 15 minutes after the end, the agent gets a safety check-in text, and with no answer in 10 minutes Sam is asked to call. A maintenance tech never goes in with only a child at home.
pf.safety.advice: Never given by Rosie: lease terms, rent deals and repair costs go to a person at the business.

pf.visit.check-in: A tour with an agent: the code at the leasing desk. Video: the agent asks for it at the start. Open house: each person's code, or the agent ticks names on the list. Self-guided: no staff; the person taps 'I've left' on the secure page, and the office checks its own lock app's log and marks it done; Rosie never connects to the lock app: staff make each one-time code there and enter it on the portal. A repair: the code at the door, or with permission to enter, DONE with a photo of the finished repair. A maintenance visit names its listed unit too; the street address and unit go only on the secure page.
pf.visit.at check-in: Pets are put away before a tech goes in. A loose pet that can't be put away: no entry, no fee, and a new time.
pf.visit.during the visit: Tours: the agent shows the home and answers from the listing details, the same way for everyone. Repairs: the booked repair only, and anything urgent found is told to the resident.
pf.visit.work changes: Another repair found at the visit is fixed only with the resident's yes, if it's quick; otherwise it's its own request. Work that needs a licensed trade goes to the office. Nothing is ever priced through Rosie.
pf.visit.what proves it's done: The code, a ticked name, the office's OK after a self-guided tour, or DONE (with a photo when nobody is home).
pf.visit.after: Tours: how to apply is the business's own process; Rosie never takes an application. Repairs: the resident can say within 24 hours if something's wrong.

pf.money.before: Nothing taken: every tour, open house spot and maintenance visit is free. No card is saved.
pf.money.after: Nothing paid through Rosie. Anything the owner charges a resident, like a repair the lease puts on the resident, is billed the business's own way, outside Rosie.
pf.money.never: No application fee, holding deposit, security deposit, rent, late fee or repair charge goes through Rosie.
pf.money.fees: None: a tour, an open house spot or a repair visit is never charged, whether it's moved, cancelled or missed.
pf.money.rosfield: $2 per confirmed booking, paid by the business on Rosfield's monthly bill, since nothing is paid through Rosie: each tour, each open house spot that checks in, each self-guided tour the office confirms, and each maintenance visit. A follow-up visit for the same repair adds no $2.

pf.messages.owner and staff texts: Texts to the owner or staff carry none of these either. Staff get entry details on the secure page.

pf.staff.leasing agents: A license or registration where the state's form asks, under the managing broker where the form says. They give tours, video tours and open houses.
pf.staff.maintenance staff: The business's own staff, with skills set per person (appliances, doors and locks, lights and fixtures). Never sent to work that needs a licensed trade.
pf.staff.who OKs what: Sam OKs everything; his answer wins. Pat, the office manager, answers requests for Lee Property Management; at Parkside Lofts only Sam does. Accommodation requests go to Sam (or Pat, for Lee Property Management), never to Rosie.
pf.staff.supervision: What a person without a license may do comes from the state's form. Safe default: set times and answer from the listing details, never talk lease terms.

pf.rules.fair housing: The same answers, times and words for everyone. No steering toward or away from a home or an area. No question or comment about a protected trait. Every disability accommodation request goes to a person. The business's fair housing notice shows where the rules require it (a switch from the state's form).
pf.rules.notice before entry: From the state's form: whether a written notice is due before staff go in, for a requested repair and with nobody home, how long ahead, and how it's given. Rosie sends it in writing.
pf.rules.leasing license: Whether a leasing agent needs a license: a switch from the state's form.
pf.rules.first step only: No leases, applications, screening, credit or background checks, rent, deposits, fees, resident notices, move-in or move-out paperwork, or outside vendors.
pf.rules.emergencies: 911 or the business's emergency line, at once. Never a booking.
pf.rules.records: Booking records 7 years by default. ID results and door codes are deleted after the business's set time (safe default: 30 days). Where the state's rules say otherwise, the form wins.

pf.edges.a home leased before the tour: The person is told at once and offered another home on the list, or a free cancel.
pf.edges.a self-guided door code that fails: The person calls the leasing office from the secure page. Nobody is let in another way.
pf.edges.someone not on the resident list asks fo: Passed to the office; nothing is booked.
pf.edges.a repair the resident may pay for: Rosie says nothing about money; the business bills its own way.
pf.edges.an accommodation request: A grab bar, an assistance animal, a parking space near the door: sent to a person. Rosie never decides, and never asks why.
pf.edges.only a child at home: The tech doesn't go in. An adult on the booking, or a new time.
pf.edges.a loose pet: No entry, a new time, never a fee.
pf.edges.an emergency at any step: 911 or the emergency line at once.

notes:
Profession 101, first step only: renter questions, tours and maintenance visits. Never leases, applications, screening, credit or background checks, rent, deposits, fees, resident notices, move-in or move-out paperwork, or outside vendors (pf.services, pf.rules first step only; A4-38, A8-44, B3-21, B3-x03, B4-03, S1-54/S1-56).
From: realtor (tours of a home with a licensed agent at a set start, fair-housing care, a free service with nothing paid through Rosie, a photo ID on the secure page, a safety check-in when no DONE comes). The realtor's tours are its flow B and its meetings its flow A, so its ops could not be copied step for step: its plug-in shape, its free-service sign-up words (S1-12 to S1-57), its off list and its fair-housing screen were adapted, and every word was rewritten. Maintenance-visit parts come from the handyman (a home visit in a 2-hour arrival window by the business's own staff, the condition photographed, nobody-home rules, DONE with a photo).
Flow A is the usual side (the person comes to the property): Parkside Lofts, Sam's apartment community run as its own company (the master's Lee's Barbershop), 240 Park Ave. Main story: Alex asks an AI Wed Oct 21 7:15pm about a 1-bedroom; Rosie answers only from the listing details (A3-x04: Unit 4B, free Nov 15, $1,450 a month as listed); a free 30-minute tour with Nina Sat Oct 24 11:00am, code 5160 at the leasing desk, DONE closes it and is Nina's safety check-in (A8-43, A8-x03).
Flow A's other tours use the master's own branches: a video tour is A4-36 (by video counts as at the business); an open house is 'a seat in a session' (S2-32/S2-33 schedule, A4-33 spots, A7-72 come any time until it ends, A7-60 Sam names the host, A8-09 names ticked); a self-guided tour is 'a space' (S2-25/S2-26 homes and windows, A4-62 windows, A4-72 the ID check on the secure page, A7-73 a window never stretches, A7-74/75 no ID by the due time, A7-38 the lock is down, own branch A8-x01/x02: the one-time door code shows only on the secure page in the window, 'I've left', Owen checks the lock's log and marks it done).
Flow B is the less usual side (the business goes to the resident): Lee Property Management (the master's Lee Home Services), 500 Main St. Main story: Alex, a resident at 14 Cedar Ln, Unit 2, asks an AI Mon Oct 19 6:40pm to fix a fridge that stopped cooling; Marcus, the business's own maintenance tech, Thu Oct 22 arriving 8-10am, code 3906 at the door; the cat is put away (B8-45); the fan motor is replaced; DONE 9:10am; nothing billed (B9-17).
Entry rules: Alex is home in the main story. A resident who will be out signs permission to enter on the secure page for that visit only (B4-26 own empty branch '3 Nobody will be home', B4-38's form branch = B4-86 permission to enter, B7-61 not signed in time, B8-69/B8-17 nobody home: DONE with a photo, B8-52/B8-53 a door code that fails). A tech never goes in with only a child home (B8-09). A loose pet that can't be put away: no entry, no fee (B8-54/B8-60).
Notice before entry is a switch from the state's form (pf.rules, pf.first_steps): the confirmation carries it where the form allows (B6-13, B4-28), and B7-30 sends a separate written notice a set time ahead where the form needs one (Kim, 24 hours). A permission or notice never carries over to a new time (B7-06, B7-28).
Door codes, entry instructions, ID details and permission details only on the secure page; staff and owner texts carry none (A6-15, A8-01, A8-x01, B6-14, B8-01, B4-34, B4-86); staff get entry details through a secure link.
Emergencies: a gas smell, fire or smoke, a smoke or carbon monoxide alarm going off, or a lockout with a child or pet inside: 911 first, then the business's emergency line; flooding, no heat in freezing weather or any other lockout: the emergency line now.
